sourceInformation.source: Pressure Cooker (Activision, 1983), designed by Garry Kitchen for Atari 2600
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js 0.180.0 / WebGPURenderer with WebGL 2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub Session Protocol 1 client 1.4.0; PeerJS 1.5.5; BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded diner with ink outlines, mint checkerboard tiles, warm coral signage and cartoon chefs
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip idle, walk, catch and dash; procedural conveyor, steam, flame and food motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written swing music at 10% default, synthesized kitchen effects and Animalese-style formant gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 shared-kitchen co-op; AI Hub authoritative shared-world sessions; standalone PeerJS Internet rooms and BroadcastChannel local rooms; same-screen keyboard and controller co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Automated core rules and full three-shift playthrough; Chromium WebGPU state checks and WebGL screenshots; emulated DualSense; touch input; WebKit mobile fallback; OfflineAudioContext output; two-page co-op; real PeerJS/WebRTC; official AI Hub harness standard, delayed/lossy, host-leave and playerless server. No physical controller, real iOS, TV or human listening test.
sourceInformation.research: Original Activision instruction manual on AtariAge; original screenshots on AtariProtos; Garry Kitchen music article; MobyGames and source sound research; official Three.js r180 sources; AI Hub README and unmodified harness

testingFeedback: 12 game, control, readability, network and packaging issues found and fixed, including lost short network actions, incorrect glyph persistence, offscreen opening orders, mouse attract exit, order identification, room editor exit, co-op departure recovery co-op restarting and mobile assist attempting the wrong chute, and a guest’s assist setting not reaching the host, missing touch reject/dash gestures, and replacement-string expansion altering the inlined JavaScript bundle.

2 critical issues: a departing co-op chef could take the final burger out of play; and JavaScript replacement-string expansion could alter compiled code while bundling. Both are fixed and covered by regression checks.

The complete ordinary-input campaign, real two-page co-op departure/restart/assist checks, and the single-file packaging assertion that caught compiled-code corruption. The official Hub harness also verified delayed networking and a playerless host.
The WebGPU screenshot was blank in headless software rendering; state checks and WebGL screenshots were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js makes a detailed procedural scene and native animation easy to combine.

The software-rendered headless WebGPU canvas could be blank while initialization and game state passed. A minimal reference scene had the same limitation; WebGL fallback screenshots rendered correctly.
The complete cooking rules, controller-first menus, synthesis and authoritative network state.
Separating a headless GPU driver limitation from game rendering errors.
More reliable headless WebGPU diagnostics and recovery after device loss.
promptFeedback: The source research and complete vertical-slice requirements give the game a clear identity.
The example four-player Hub stress test exceeds a declared two-player game; the same scenarios are run with two players.
Combining controller-first UX, readable kitchen action and both standalone and Hub co-op in a single file.
Specify a preferred multiplayer player count and whether headless WebGPU screenshot limitations should use the WebGL fallback.

aiHub.name: Pressure Buns
aiHub.description: Catch flying toppings, stack exact orders on a moving belt, and rush burgers to their matching wrappers. Run three increasingly busy shifts solo or share the kitchen with a friend.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD: move; × / E: serve; □ / Q: reject; ○ / Space: dash; Options / Esc: pause; mouse click: walk and act; touch: drag to move.
